qualification: Proved on in-memory ledgers and an in-memory pool whose BEGIN/ROLLBACK keep and restore the rows. No database, object store, dispatcher loop or served HTTP walk was run.
defect: ZL1 limit 1: a large ZIP layer's zip-layer/1 lineage was merged into sources.inspection.archiveMember in a transaction after finalize; a crash between the two kept the child without its lineage and the member unlinked, and enrolling the archive again kept the member a second time.
decisions: D1 large-original.ts: finalize takes an optional fourth argument, archiveMember, validated by LargeLayerLineageSchema (the zip-layer/1 schema ZL1 used, now exported beside finalize; memberBytes bounded by STREAMING_VECTOR_LIMITS.sourceBytes) before any statement, and writes it into the new source's inspection.archiveMember inside the transaction that inserts the source. A lineage given for a large-original/2 receipt is refused ARCHIVE_MEMBER_PROFILE before any change, because v2 publishes in its storage job. The /uploads controller passes three arguments, so its inspection and behaviour are unchanged; the HTTP finalize schema and the published contract are unchanged.

D2 intake-zip-layers.ts: keepLargeLayer passes the lineage to receiveLargeLayer, which passes it to finalize; the separate UPDATE sources is gone; linking the member item stays a transaction of its own. A finalize that fails leaves the receipt aborted (or expiring as today) and the member unlinked with its words, so enrolling again opens one new receipt and keeps the member once.
D3 no contract field, no schema step; pins moved for the two source files only.

D4 (lead, after acceptance) intake-zip-layers.ts linkKeptTx: before any member byte is read, keepLayer looks for a source in the case whose inspection.archiveMember contains the same parentSourceId, parentSourceRevision, parentSha256 and memberPath and whose own sha256 equals that lineage's memberSha256 (earliest by created_at, id), and links the member to it in the same transaction. The member's SHA-256 cannot be known before streaming; the parent's revision and SHA-256 pin the member's bytes, and the child's SHA-256 matching its recorded memberSha256 stands for that check. Small layers take the same rule, because their retain (service.ts) records the same lineage in the transaction that inserts the source.
